bull_bear.body: Management explicitly does **not** want to grow leverage beyond the current 0.6x debt-to-equity; any "healthy capital infusion" required for the Brands-of-Brand mass expansion would be funded via **preferential allotment or equity**, timed to when the capex requirement "arises immediately" rather than pre-funded now. No dividend or buyback discussed.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Execution gap between plan and current scale** — 1 EBO today vs. a 50-store two-year target and 300–400-store five-year ambition; no signed airport leases yet.
- **EBITDA margin compression (−190bps YoY)** from input-cost inflation — management's "prices have normalized" claim for cotton/yarn is a forward assumption, not yet proven across a full year.
- **New licensing-cost commitment (~Rs 6–8cr/year MG)** is a real, incremental fixed cost tied to a still-unbuilt retail concept — a drag on margins before the offsetting revenue materializes.
- **B2B debtor cycle (3–4 months, targeted to 90–100 days)** remains a structural working-capital drag typical of the garment trade; reduction is a stated goal, not yet achieved.
- **Geographic concentration** — Kidcity's shop-in-shop base is heavily Eastern-India-concentrated; expansion into Central India (MP) is only beginning.
- **No independent competitive moat evidence beyond management's own claim** of vertically-integrated cost advantage over FirstCry/Hopscotch-style aggregator peers — plausible given the stated business model difference, but not externally verified.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: CFO Krishan Karnani is unusually transparent and granular — walks through exact brand names, buying-house trade mechanics, per-store capex/inventory/break-even economics, and specific MG licensing costs without prompting, and concedes directly when data isn't available (e.g., precise regional sales bifurcation, given bill-to/ship-to limitations). He is candid that airport locations are expected to be break-even-at-best (a visibility play, not a profit center) rather than overselling the concept. The founder/MD's opening remarks (highest-ever revenue/EBITDA/PAT, main-board migration) are promotional in framing but consistent with the disclosed numbers.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The white-labeling pivot appears to be working as a Trojan horse for own-brand orders** — management's specific anecdote (large corporates placing simultaneous own-brand orders once white-labeled, especially visible in this quarter's Puja-season sales) is a concrete, checkable claim for whether this dynamic repeats in subsequent festive quarters.
- **Airport retail is explicitly NOT expected to be profitable on its own** — a rare instance of management proactively lowering expectations on a flagship new-growth-vertical component rather than overselling it, with profitability instead expected to accrue to mall/online channels via the brand-recall halo effect.
- **The "Brands of Brand" concept is explicitly original to the Indian market** per management ("one of a kind concept which India doesn't have") — if true, this is a genuine white-space claim worth testing against any competitor activity in subsequent quarters, though currently unverified beyond management's own assertion.
- **FY29–30 targets (Rs 500cr Kidcity revenue, ~1,000 SIS + 300–400 EBO stores) are 3+ years out and highly aggressive relative to the current single-EBO base** — useful as a long-range marker, but should be weighted far less than the FY27/FY28 near-term targets when assessing credibility.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net Debt-to-Equity has been reduced sharply from 2.8x (FY23) to 0.8x (FY26), per the deleveraging chart.
- Raised funds via an SME IPO used for debt reduction, working capital support and modernisation initiatives, followed by NSE Emerge listing; also completed a 1:4 bonus share issue in 2026, per the company timeline.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- customer lock-in: repeat customers account for more than 90 percent of business, with over 90% of revenue from clients retained three years or more — evidence: "repeat customers now account for more than 90 percent of business" / "Over 90% of revenue now comes from clients who have stuck around for three years or more"
- scale: eleven-plus garment categories manufactured under one roof lets a single retailer source nearly its entire kidswear order from Karnika alone — evidence: "Eleven-plus garment categories, spanning shorts, joggers, capris, tees, rompers, sleep suits, winter wear, infant wear, fancy suits, girls' separates, and jumpsuits, sit under one manufacturing roof"
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material (cotton) price risk — Cotton is the key raw material and fluctuations in its price can impact realizations and profitability.
- Geographic concentration in Howrah — All manufacturing currently sits in Howrah, so any disruption local to that region carries outsized risk, and geographic scale-up would require building fresh capacity elsewhere.
- Elevated receivables / working capital pressure — Debtor days increased to 158 days and the cash conversion cycle remains elevated (~269 days), suggesting potential liquidity strains; working capital pressure from elevated receivables could tighten cash flow if market conditions turn.
- Low export share leaves international opportunity largely untapped — Exports make up a small slice of total business today, leaving the international opportunity mostly untouched.
- Tariff and trade-policy risk on exports — Tariff changes, including potential U.S. duties on textiles, alongside broader geopolitical and supply chain disruption, could hit export economics without warning.
- Inflation risk on costs — Variable inflation trends in India can present challenges in forecasting and managing raw material and employee benefit costs.
- Credit / finance risk from customer receivables — Credit risk is managed based on market-condition assumptions; the Company tracks debtor creditworthiness through internal systems configured to define customer credit limits.
- Competitive pressure from organized and unorganized manufacturers — Organized manufacturers with scale and a large field of nimble local players both compete hard for the same customers.

business.body:
- **Karnika (B2B, parent brand):** H1 revenue ~Rs 140cr, 98% own-brand / 2% white-label; sells through large buying houses (arhats) into a multi-tier wholesale/retail chain; ~eight registered sub-brands (Karnika Cool/Life/Ring/Key/Cube etc.) differentiated by age-group/size/price point; WSP (wholesale selling price) typically Rs 150–500; inventory returns <1% given "value for money," fast-moving product positioning.
- **Kidcity (B2C, acquired subsidiary):** four revenue models — (1) shop-in-shop (85+ outlets, MRP Rs 199–499, targeting Tier-2/3/4), (2) aggregation (sole Kolkata aggregator for Hopscotch; also works with Styli/Landmark Group, Bumpzee), (3) B2B/white-labeling under the "Ojos" brand (incl. for FirstCry, Style Baazar, V-Mart, Vishal), (4) new "Brands of Brand" EBO/kiosk concept (licensed-character merchandise, MRP Rs 799–1,499, targeting Tier-1/2 airports and malls). Geographic concentration for shop-in-shop currently Eastern India (West Bengal, Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar), now expanding into the Central India/MP belt.
- **FirstCry relationship:** Karnika supplies FirstCry's private-label brands (Mark & Mia, Ed-a-Mamma, Disney) as a white-label manufacturer — management frames FirstCry/peers as themselves outsourcing to factories like Karnika's, positioning Karnika's owned fabric-sourcing-to-manufacturing vertical integration as a structural cost/economics advantage over "brand-only" competitors.
- **Regional mix (B2B):** ~55% North & West India, ~45% Central & South India — based on billing address of the buying house, which management notes may not reflect final consumption geography precisely (bill-to/ship-to practices vary by buying house).

outlook.body:
- **FY28 guidance (reaffirmed):** revenue and PBT CAGR **30–35% through FY28**, EBITDA margin range **17–20%**.
- **Raw-material/margin outlook:** cotton/yarn prices have "normalized" at their new, higher level — management expects **no further increase** through Q3/Q4FY27 and margins to hold broadly in the **18–19%** range (within the 17–20% guided band) for the full year; cost pass-through to customers runs with roughly a one-quarter lag (absorbed the Q1 hit, passed it on from Q2).
- **Kidcity revenue targets:** **Rs 80–100cr for FY27**; **Rs 180–200cr for FY28**; **Rs 500cr by FY29–30** (internal long-range target) — alongside **~1,000 shop-in-shop counters** and **300–400 EBO/kiosk outlets** by FY29–30. Kidcity PAT margin targeted at **10–13%.**
- **Karnika (B2B) standalone growth:** expected to continue at its "standard" **20–25% YoY**, with Kidcity as the larger incremental growth driver of the blended 30–35% target.
- **"Brands of Brand" EBO/kiosk rollout:** **~50 stores planned across FY27–FY28** (airports + high-street malls); per-store economics targeted at **Rs 50 lakh/year revenue at 13–14% margin**; break-even for shop-in-shop stores in **9–12 months.**
- **Debtor-day reduction:** B2B payment cycle currently ~3–4 months, targeted down to **90–100 days.**
- **Cross-store exchange technology** (buy at one city's outlet, exchange at another) targeted for completion by **Feb/March 2027.**
- **Airport negotiations:** active discussions with GMR (Delhi), Kolkata Airport, and Lucknow Airport for initial "Brands of Brand" sites — no signed leases disclosed yet.

White-labeling customers for Karnika brand include Vishal, V-Mart, V2, Styli; B2B retail-chain customers cited: Style Baazar, FirstCry, Srijan, Hopscotch.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **"Brands of Brand" licensed-character retail concept** — airport + high-street mall kiosks selling branded character merchandise (e.g., Disney, Marvel, Panda) plus margin-accretive accessories (bottles, purses, hair bands); management frames airport locations as **break-even-at-best, brand-visibility plays**, with actual profitability expected from mall/online channels once customers recall airport exposure. ~12 licensed-character brands currently projected, with **minimum-guarantee (MG) licensing costs of ~Rs 6–8cr/year** in aggregate (e.g., Disney alone ~Rs 50–80 lakh/year MG) — a real, quantified new cost line tied to this expansion.
- **White-labeling pivot (Karnika):** previously declined, now actively pursued — management credits this quarter's own-brand order strength partly to large corporate clients simultaneously placing own-brand orders once a white-label relationship is established (cited specifically around this quarter's festive/Puja-season sales).
- **Long-run own-IP ambition:** management states that once Kidcity stores are profitable and running, the company intends to develop its **own original character** for in-house branding, rather than relying solely on licensed third-party IP.

- Focus on strengthening manufacturing capabilities and global footprint
- Vertically integrated garment manufacturing to enable consistent quality, cost efficiency and supply chain reliability
- Entry into the D2C/SIS model sector via the Kidcity Solutions acquisition, beyond the core export business
- Domestic focus on design-led, branded kidswear rather than pure volume manufacturing
- Promote employee well-being, continuous learning and workplace diversity through upskilling and wellness programs

outlook.body: Karnika describes future growth as funded by growth capital directed at product quality, operational efficiency and market reach, with investment in innovative fabrics, eco-friendly practices and advanced manufacturing. The Company acquired 75% of Kidcity Solutions Private Limited during the quarter ending December 2025, giving it entry into the D2C/SIS model sector alongside its core export garment business. outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Manufacturer serving both domestic and export markets remains attentive to input costs, freight/logistics expenses and shifts in global demand
- Global apparel sourcing landscape shifting away from China toward hubs including India, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Thailand and Sri Lanka, benefiting India-based garment manufacturers
- India's textile and apparel industry shifting from volume-led growth toward value-added categories, consistent with the Company's design-led branded kidswear focus
- India-UK Free Trade Agreement (July 2025) provides duty-free access for Indian textile exports, closing a 10-12% tariff gap with competing exporters, seen as relevant to the Company's product categories
- Trade agreements with the US, UK and UAE expected to boost India's export competitiveness going forward
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: A genuinely strong quarter — **highest-ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT** (revenue +52.3% YoY to Rs 106cr) — driven by a strategic shift to accept white-labeling for large retail chains (which management says pulled in parallel own-brand orders) and the scaling B2C arm Kidcity, even as **EBITDA margin compressed ~190bps YoY** (18.8% vs 20.7%) on cotton/yarn and dyeing-chemical cost inflation not yet fully passed through. The quarter's headline corporate milestone — **eligibility for migration to the main board** effective 13-Oct-2026 — coincides with an ambitious, still largely pre-revenue retail build-out plan (a new licensed-character "Brands of Brand" airport/mall concept targeting 50 stores by FY28 and Rs 500cr Kidcity revenue by FY29-30) that is long on specifics but entirely unexecuted today (Kidcity currently has just **1 EBO**, in Purnia).

open.item: Growth capital will drive sustainable expansion, focused on product quality, operational efficiency, and market reach, with investment in innovative fabrics, eco-friendly practices and advanced manufacturing.
Export growth, supply chain optimization and brand visibility will reinforce Karnika's position as a design-driven leader in children's apparel.
Cotton price fluctuations can impact realizations and profitability; the Company mitigates this through prudent sourcing, efficient inventory management and continuous operational improvements.

qoq_log.body:
- **Q2 FY27 (this):** Revenue Rs 106cr (+52.3% YoY, highest-ever quarterly); EBITDA margin 18.8% (down from 20.7% on input-cost inflation); PAT Rs 14cr (+51% YoY); working capital days improved to 143 (H1) from 178 (FY26). Main-board migration eligibility achieved (effective 13-Oct-2026). White-labeling pivot credited for own-brand order strength. "Brands of Brand" EBO concept launched conceptually (1 EBO live, in Purnia); 50-store FY27-28 target and Rs500cr/1,000+SIS/300-400 EBO FY29-30 long-range target disclosed; airport site talks (GMR Delhi, Kolkata, Lucknow) in progress, unsigned.
- _Q3 FY27 → check: EBITDA margin trajectory as cotton/yarn prices "normalize"; actual EBO/kiosk store additions against the 50-store FY27-28 target; airport lease signings; debtor-day reduction progress toward 90-100 days; Kidcity revenue tracking against the Rs80-100cr FY27 target._

one-line thesis: A genuinely strong quarter — highest-ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT (revenue +52.3% YoY to Rs 106cr) — driven by a strategic shift to accept white-labeling for large retail chains (which management says pulled in parallel own-brand orders) and the scaling B2C arm Kidcity, even as EBITDA margin compressed ~190bps YoY (18.8% vs 20.7%) on cotton/yarn and dyeing-chemical cost inflation not yet fully passed through. The quarter's headline corporate milestone — eligibility for migration to the main board effective 13-Oct-2026 — coincides with an ambitious, still largely pre-revenue retail build-out plan (a new licensed-character "Brands of Brand" airport/mall concept targeting 50 stores by FY28 and Rs 500cr Kidcity revenue by FY29-30) that is long on specifics but entirely unexecuted today (Kidcity currently has just 1 EBO, in Purnia).
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > Revenue split H1FY27: Karnika (B2B) Rs 140cr; Kidcity (B2C) Rs 40cr; consolidated Rs 180cr. Own-brand mix 98% / white-labeling 2% (Vishal, V-Mart, V2, Styli, Hopscotch).
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: FY28 guidance (reaffirmed): revenue and PBT CAGR 30–35% through FY28, EBITDA margin range 17–20%.

Raw-material/margin outlook: cotton/yarn prices have "normalized" at their new, higher level — management expects no further increase through Q3/Q4FY27 and margins to hold broadly in the 18–19% range (within the 17–20% guided band) for the full year; cost pass-through to customers runs with roughly a one-quarter lag (absorbed the Q1 hit, passed it on from Q2).

Kidcity revenue targets: Rs 80–100cr for FY27; Rs 180–200cr for FY28; Rs 500cr by FY29–30 (internal long-range target) — alongside ~1,000 shop-in-shop counters and 300–400 EBO/kiosk outlets by FY29–30. Kidcity PAT margin targeted at 10–13%.
Karnika (B2B) standalone growth: expected to continue at its "standard" 20–25% YoY, with Kidcity as the larger incremental growth driver of the blended 30–35% target.

"Brands of Brand" EBO/kiosk rollout: ~50 stores planned across FY27–FY28 (airports + high-street malls); per-store economics targeted at Rs 50 lakh/year revenue at 13–14% margin; break-even for shop-in-shop stores in 9–12 months.
Debtor-day reduction: B2B payment cycle currently ~3–4 months, targeted down to 90–100 days.
Cross-store exchange technology (buy at one city's outlet, exchange at another) targeted for completion by Feb/March 2027.
Airport negotiations: active discussions with GMR (Delhi), Kolkata Airport, and Lucknow Airport for initial "Brands of Brand" sites — no signed leases disclosed yet.
order book & pipeline: B2B model is purely sell-through (via large "buying houses"/arhats, each with turnover of Rs 500cr–5,000cr, who then distribute pan-India to wholesalers and retailers) — no discrete order book disclosed. Pipeline for Kidcity: 85+ shop-in-shop counters live in H1FY27 (operating inside Spencers, Rustees, Chennai Silks, and regional family-retail chains in Bihar/Odisha); 1 operational EBO; target of 55+ kiosks at airports/premium high-street locations; aggregation deals with Hopscotch (sole Kolkata-goods aggregator for them) and Styli (Landmark Group) plus a newer Bumpzee relationship. White-labeling customers for Karnika brand include Vishal, V-Mart, V2, Styli; B2B retail-chain customers cited: Style Baazar, FirstCry, Srijan, Hopscotch.
segment / subsidiary detail: Karnika (B2B, parent brand): H1 revenue ~Rs 140cr, 98% own-brand / 2% white-label; sells through large buying houses (arhats) into a multi-tier wholesale/retail chain; ~eight registered sub-brands (Karnika Cool/Life/Ring/Key/Cube etc.) differentiated by age-group/size/price point; WSP (wholesale selling price) typically Rs 150–500; inventory returns <1% given "value for money," fast-moving product positioning.

Kidcity (B2C, acquired subsidiary): four revenue models — (1) shop-in-shop (85+ outlets, MRP Rs 199–499, targeting Tier-2/3/4), (2) aggregation (sole Kolkata aggregator for Hopscotch; also works with Styli/Landmark Group, Bumpzee), (3) B2B/white-labeling under the "Ojos" brand (incl. for FirstCry, Style Baazar, V-Mart, Vishal), (4) new "Brands of Brand" EBO/kiosk concept (licensed-character merchandise, MRP Rs 799–1,499, targeting Tier-1/2 airports and malls). Geographic concentration for shop-in-shop currently Eastern India (West Bengal, Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar), now expanding into the Central India/MP belt.

FirstCry relationship: Karnika supplies FirstCry's private-label brands (Mark & Mia, Ed-a-Mamma, Disney) as a white-label manufacturer — management frames FirstCry/peers as themselves outsourcing to factories like Karnika's, positioning Karnika's owned fabric-sourcing-to-manufacturing vertical integration as a structural cost/economics advantage over "brand-only" competitors.

Regional mix (B2B): ~55% North & West India, ~45% Central & South India — based on billing address of the buying house, which management notes may not reflect final consumption geography precisely (bill-to/ship-to practices vary by buying house).
growth verticals / optionality: "Brands of Brand" licensed-character retail concept — airport + high-street mall kiosks selling branded character merchandise (e.g., Disney, Marvel, Panda) plus margin-accretive accessories (bottles, purses, hair bands); management frames airport locations as break-even-at-best, brand-visibility plays, with actual profitability expected from mall/online channels once customers recall airport exposure. ~12 licensed-character brands currently projected, with minimum-guarantee (MG) licensing costs of ~Rs 6–8cr/year in aggregate (e.g., Disney alone ~Rs 50–80 lakh/year MG) — a real, quantified new cost line tied to this expansion.

White-labeling pivot (Karnika): previously declined, now actively pursued — management credits this quarter's own-brand order strength partly to large corporate clients simultaneously placing own-brand orders once a white-label relationship is established (cited specifically around this quarter's festive/Puja-season sales).

Long-run own-IP ambition: management states that once Kidcity stores are profitable and running, the company intends to develop its own original character for in-house branding, rather than relying solely on licensed third-party IP.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin compressed to 18.8% (Q2, from 20.7%) and 18.2% (H1, from 18.9%) purely on input-cost inflation (yarn, dyeing chemicals, processing charges) — management states cost increases were "taken as a hard hit" in Q1 and then passed through to customers from Q2 onward, with a structural ~1-quarter lag between cost increases and pricing pass-through. PAT margin held broadly stable (13.4% vs 13.5% Q2; 13% vs 12.1% H1, actually improving) despite the EBITDA-margin compression — implying some offset below the EBITDA line (not specifically detailed on the call, e.g. depreciation/finance-cost leverage from H1 scale growth).
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Shop-in-shop (SIS): ~Rs 2–3 lakh capex + Rs 3–5 lakh inventory per store; break-even 9–12 months.
"Brands of Brand" EBO/kiosk: ~Rs 10–15 lakh capex + Rs 10–15 lakh inventory per store; targeted ~Rs 50 lakh/year revenue at 13–14% margin per store once mature.

Karnika (B2B) manufacturing: minimal incremental capex expected — last year's SEDEX-compliant unit already completed; expansion capacity exists in-house plus via job-work, with no capacity constraint flagged.

Watch slippage: only 1 EBO currently operational (Purnia) against a stated 50-store, two-year (FY27–28) rollout plan and a 300–400-store, five-year (FY29–30) ambition — this is the single largest execution gap between stated plan and current reality in this call. Airport site negotiations (GMR Delhi, Kolkata, Lucknow) are still in talks, not signed.
capital allocation: Management explicitly does not want to grow leverage beyond the current 0.6x debt-to-equity; any "healthy capital infusion" required for the Brands-of-Brand mass expansion would be funded via preferential allotment or equity, timed to when the capex requirement "arises immediately" rather than pre-funded now. No dividend or buyback discussed.
risks & watch-items: Execution gap between plan and current scale — 1 EBO today vs. a 50-store two-year target and 300–400-store five-year ambition; no signed airport leases yet.
EBITDA margin compression (−190bps YoY) from input-cost inflation — management's "prices have normalized" claim for cotton/yarn is a forward assumption, not yet proven across a full year.
New licensing-cost commitment (~Rs 6–8cr/year MG) is a real, incremental fixed cost tied to a still-unbuilt retail concept — a drag on margins before the offsetting revenue materializes.
B2B debtor cycle (3–4 months, targeted to 90–100 days) remains a structural working-capital drag typical of the garment trade; reduction is a stated goal, not yet achieved.
Geographic concentration — Kidcity's shop-in-shop base is heavily Eastern-India-concentrated; expansion into Central India (MP) is only beginning.

No independent competitive moat evidence beyond management's own claim of vertically-integrated cost advantage over FirstCry/Hopscotch-style aggregator peers — plausible given the stated business model difference, but not externally verified.
management quality / tone: CFO Krishan Karnani is unusually transparent and granular — walks through exact brand names, buying-house trade mechanics, per-store capex/inventory/break-even economics, and specific MG licensing costs without prompting, and concedes directly when data isn't available (e.g., precise regional sales bifurcation, given bill-to/ship-to limitations). He is candid that airport locations are expected to be break-even-at-best (a visibility play, not a profit center) rather than overselling the concept. The founder/MD's opening remarks (highest-ever revenue/EBITDA/PAT, main-board migration) are promotional in framing but consistent with the disclosed numbers.
non-obvious takeaways: The white-labeling pivot appears to be working as a Trojan horse for own-brand orders — management's specific anecdote (large corporates placing simultaneous own-brand orders once white-labeled, especially visible in this quarter's Puja-season sales) is a concrete, checkable claim for whether this dynamic repeats in subsequent festive quarters.

Airport retail is explicitly NOT expected to be profitable on its own — a rare instance of management proactively lowering expectations on a flagship new-growth-vertical component rather than overselling it, with profitability instead expected to accrue to mall/online channels via the brand-recall halo effect.

The "Brands of Brand" concept is explicitly original to the Indian market per management ("one of a kind concept which India doesn't have") — if true, this is a genuine white-space claim worth testing against any competitor activity in subsequent quarters, though currently unverified beyond management's own assertion.

FY29–30 targets (Rs 500cr Kidcity revenue, ~1,000 SIS + 300–400 EBO stores) are 3+ years out and highly aggressive relative to the current single-EBO base — useful as a long-range marker, but should be weighted far less than the FY27/FY28 near-term targets when assessing credibility.

themes.title: Textiles - apparel/home-textile exports + synthetics
themes.need: India textiles ride three tailwinds at once: China+1 sourcing shifts, the India-UK FTA (signed) + India-EU FTA (advancing), and US tariff normalization - favouring apparel exporters (GOKEX/PGIL/PDSL) and US-heavy home-textile names (WELSPUNLIV/HIMATSEIDE). A second leg = value-added synthetics/recycling (FILATEX, SANATHAN, CENTENKA, GANECOS) and cotton-yarn spread recovery (VTL/NITINSPIN/SPORTKING) plus branded apparel (PAGEIND, ARVIND, RAYMONDLSL).
themes.driver: FTA implementation + US-India trade-deal clarity; festive/wedding demand; cotton-yarn spread; anti-dumping rulings.
